role: Spelled-number normaliser for the assistant's claim checks: rewrites spelled-out numbers in a reply ('negative thirty-one point seven', 'one hundred and sixty', 'one-sixty') to digits, recording each rewrite so a range found in the digit-form text can be mapped back to the original. Used by MetricsVerifier (and, through MetricsVerifier.normalizeSpelledNumbers, UserAssertedValuesParser).
types: SpelledNumberNormalizer: enum — namespace of the normaliser
SpelledNumberNormalizer.Rewrite: struct — original vs normalized NSRange of one spelled-number rewrite
state: static let onesAndTeens / tens (word->int maps for spelled numbers)
toplevel: The onesAndTeens / tens word maps. The pattern is compiled through DebugLogger.compiledPattern, which caches and logs a compile failure.

units.does: Rewrites each spelled-number match into digits via spelledNumberReplacement ('negative thirty-one point seven' -> '-31.7', 'one hundred and sixty' -> '160', 'one-sixty' -> '160', 'point seven five' -> '.75'), recording original/normalized ranges for every rewrite; returns the input unchanged with no rewrites if the pattern does not compile. Every spelled number is rewritten, but only for matching: callers map ranges back and correct the original text.
Maps a normalized-text UTF-16 offset to the original: accumulates shift from rewrites ending before it; an offset strictly inside a rewrite snaps to the rewrite's original start or end.

branches.cond: offset inside the rewrite (after its start)

units.does: Builds the spelled-number regex string from onesAndTeens (longest first), tens and digit words: optional 'negative', then the first of a hundreds form ('a|<digit> hundred [and] <below-hundred>'), the hyphenated 'one|two-<tens>[-<digit>]' form, or a below-hundred number (tens[-ones] | ones/teen), then optional 'point' followed by one or more digit words.

Turns one matched phrase into its digit string: splits on whitespace and '-', drops 'negative' and 'and', reads the integer part (spelledInteger) before 'point' and concatenates each digit word after it, prefixing '-' when the phrase starts with 'negative'. Nil when a word is not a number word.

Integer value of number words: 'hundred' multiplies what came before (at least 1); 'a' is 1; a tens word after a lone ones word 1-9 with no 'hundred' is the 'one-sixty' form (ones*100 + tens); otherwise tens and ones/teens add. Nil for an empty list or a non-number word.

branches.effect: ones*100+tens when value is 1-9 and no hundred yet, else adds
